note: The standing red set on main. It is a statement about main, not a gate: a red name that is not in this list is REPORTED loudly by the round and written to the round log, and does not refuse anybody’s change. The one thing that does stop a round is a change that REMOVES a name from this list while that test is still red — taking a name out is the claim that it came good. Adding one is raising the floor and is meant to be reviewed as such. See docs/mc-command-matrix.md. 2026-08-30, re-seeded from a full suite run: 70 → 32. Of the 38 that left, 14 went with the session verbs whose tests were deleted and cannot come back; 11 were never broken at all (a fixture compared /var against its /private symlink); 13 are broker tests that were red only because the local codex install was missing its platform binary — those can go red again on a machine without codex, and under this file’s rules that is a warning about main, not a refusal. Seven file-level names are back after the gate refused to let them go: a full run names those failures per test, a selected run names them per file, and both spellings are true. The floor carries both, which is why it has always been larger than the count of distinct failures. 2026-09-01, 38 → 31: `mc spawn` and the two grounding assertions. Neither was a test that broke — both were assertions outliving their subject, the way readPackageCanon outlived the heading it checked. The gate refuses on any red the selection reaches, so a stale assertion in a widely imported module is a standing veto over unrelated work.
